test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, angle PSQ = 125 degrees and angle PRT = 110 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle SPR?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fba347fdce920ec546deb95bd88b54a12469c78833c108144a64daa43127337.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of any two exterior angles of a triangle = 180° + Interior angle of the third vertex.

∠PSQ + ∠PRT = 180° + ∠SPR

125° + 110° = 180° + ∠SPR

235° = 180° + ∠SPR

∠SPR = 235° − 180° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97cffc03acc12ff2cb6b45778ceddc8430b860360f8533631e7fa9f55661e01e.png] 

Given: ∠PSQ = 125° and ∠PRT = 110°

∠PSR and ∠PSQ form a linear pair on line QR.

⇒ ∠PSR + ∠PSQ = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR + 125° = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR = 180° − 125° = 55°

Similarly, ∠PRS and ∠PRT form a linear pair on line ST.

⇒ ∠PRS + ∠PRT = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS + 110° = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS = 180° − 110° = 70°

In ΔSPR, by Angle Sum Property:

⇒ ∠SPR + ∠PSR + ∠PRS = 180°

⇒ ∠SPR + 55° + 70° = 180°

⇒ ∠SPR + 125° = 180°

⇒ ∠SPR = 180° − 125° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. For ΔSPR, ∠PSQ = ∠SPR + ∠PRS.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°.
